title: MemoryBackend::demo_next_id diverges from canonical mail-server's uuid-based create_object
description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/memory.rs:193-235 implements MemoryBackend::demo_next_id with a two-mode helper (deterministic len()-based default, or realistic-demo-ids feature for a process-global timestamp+counter). The canonical mail-server (crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:961-979) does NOT use demo_next_id; it uses uuid::Uuid::new_v4() directly inside create_object. The canonical's pattern is collision-free and persistent-across-restarts ish; the sharing sibling's default mode has documented collision-on-delete (per the inline comment at memory.rs:215-220 and the workspace-tracked bead bd:JMAP-qz9v.14).

Per workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates': if a sibling reshapes its impl in a way that diverges from the canonical, the canonical changes first then the sibling propagates. The reverse is a regression of cookie-cutter intent.

The 920fb0d commit landed demo_next_id in 6 siblings (chat, calendars, contacts, metadata, sharing, tasks) but explicitly excluded mail-server. The commit message acknowledges the workspace-wide drift as a deliberate mitigation against cargo-culting the worse mail-server pattern — but that reverses the canonical-template precedence rule.

Two resolutions:
  (a) Propagate demo_next_id to mail-server's create_object as the new canonical (drop uuid::Uuid::new_v4()).
  (b) Revert the 6 siblings to use uuid::Uuid::new_v4() matching the canonical (then revisit the cargo-cult concern that motivated 920fb0d).

Neither is a one-line fix. This is the meta-finding the cookie-cutter rule says review should catch. Cross-references: bd:JMAP-qz9v.14, bd:JMAP-826m.18, bd:JMAP-qz9v.47, bd:JMAP-qz9v.46, bd:JMAP-ayoz.20, bd:JMAP-x2gd.63.
notes:
DECISION NEEDED (triage 2026-10-19 at 9fdbbbcf): Question for Mark: should the extension-server MemoryBackend id minting follow canonical mail-server's uuid v4, or should demo_next_id become the convention?

Options:
(a) Make demo_next_id canonical. Add demo_next_id, with contacts-server's monotonic next_ids default and the realistic-demo-ids feature, to mail-server's create_object and replace uuid::Uuid::new_v4 there. This adds a feature to mail-server (not breaking) and adds moving parts to the canonical.
(b) Use uuid v4 everywhere. Delete demo_next_id, the next_ids counters, the debug_asserts and the realistic-demo-ids feature from the 5 siblings, add the uuid dependency, and call Uuid::new_v4 in create_object, matching mail-server. This breaks API because a published cargo feature is removed. It needs a few deterministic-id test literals in calendars, chat and contacts replaced with ids taken from the create responses. It also makes JMAP-h7jp moot, since there is no counter left to collide.
(c) Record a documented exception. Add an AGENTS.md note, like the existing max_<thing> 'older pattern, NOT retroactively reshaped' note: mail-server's uuid minting predates the convention, demo_next_id with the contacts-style monotonic counter is the extension-sibling convention, and neither is propagated to the other. Then close this bead as a decision and widen JMAP-h7jp to cover sharing and tasks too, since both still have the len() collision.

Recommendation: (b). It removes a whole category of code (a feature flag, two cfg modes, counters, collision asserts and the JMAP-h7jp sweep) and puts the workspace back on the canonical. Removing the feature is a small break in pre-1.0 demo backends. If deterministic ids matter for testjig snapshots or docs, choose (c), the cheapest documented constraint, rather than (a).
DECIDED by Mark 2026-10-19: option (b). All MemoryBackends mint ids with uuid v4 like canonical mail-server. Delete demo_next_id, next_ids counters, collision debug_asserts and the realistic-demo-ids feature from the 5 siblings; tests read ids from create responses instead of literals. Makes JMAP-h7jp moot (close it). Breaking (feature removed), 0.3.0.
close_reason: Landed as 2a8bf0aa (uuid v4 MemoryBackend ids; realistic-demo-ids feature removed). Review passed. CI green at 8e240e18 (stable+beta 3502 passed).
